newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France launches alliance with U.S. carriers.
newsitem.headline: Air France launches alliance with U.S. carriers.

text.p: Air France announced on Monday the start of a transatlantic alliance with two major U.S. carriers, Delta Air Lines and Continental, part of a strategy to form global links vital to the French state-owned carrier's future.

To mark the beginning of the alliance, announced last October, Delta and Continental began transferring their flights and operations to Air France's central hub at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport from Paris Orly.
Under the move, Air France will be linked to five major U.S. hubs -- New York's JFK airport, Atlanta and Cincinnati belonging to Delta and New York-Newark and Houston belonging to Continental.
As part of the deal, the airlines plan to link their schedules more closely.
"These agreements are aimed at the creation of a truly global network," Air France said in a statement.

Air France added that, subject to French and U.S. government approval, the deal would eventually allow for code-sharing among the airlines which is a low-cost way of gaining more customers without direct investment by using partners' networks.

It means passengers can be issued with a through ticket by one carrier to be used on its partner airline -- making it possible for airlines to feed passenbers to each other without having to invest in their own routes.
More than three million passengers travel between the United States and France every year.
Air France, facing increased competition in regional markets, has said it intends to build a global network of alliances to ensure its survival.
The airline officially lost its national monopoly status on April 1, when domestic air travel in the European Union was opened up to competition from European carriers.
The airline expects to break even in 1997, paving the way for its privatisation later this year or early in 1998.
But the carrier has been hit by major labour unrest over efforts to make it more competitive and cut costs.
